page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 4 vCPUs, mapped to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, and 15 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The underlying hardware features a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, supported by a 45 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. In stress-ng CPU evaluations, both single-core and multi-core performance fall within the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show similar constraints, with read-only large block transfers reaching 25.29 GB/sec and write operations at 21.61 GB/sec. Complex tasks like software compilation via Clang and ray tracing also register in the bottom 25%, while text processing and single-threaded gzip compression drop to the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-4 represents a legacy hardware profile that trades raw processing power for a balanced resource allocation. The dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable execution times compared to shared-core alternatives, but the older architecture limits its throughput-per-resource ratio. This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and small-scale database operations that do not require high-speed local storage or advanced vector instructions.
